cand.title: Toronto–Montreal group and team-building incentive programmes
cand.excerpt: Toronto-headquartered DMC publicly markets group tours, incentive programmes, conferences and events, and identifies Toronto as an incentive start/end destination. Its meetings offering covers incentive design, corporate events and conference arrangements, making it a relevant intermediary for Toronto hotel, meeting and banquet referrals.
linkedLedgerProgrammes: Canadian Tours International (CTI Destination Management) — Toronto–Montreal group and team-building incentive programmes

quote.assumption: exa agent fixed effort=high (contact enrichment not included)

findings.namedBuyers: Michelle Kenny, VP of Operations, and Terry Engesser, Managing Director (also identified as President by the representation partner), are verified commercially relevant CTI contacts. Michelle is the logical first operational qualification contact; Terry is the senior supplier-relationship escalation. Their roles do not establish authority to sign hotel contracts for any specific client or programme.
findings.futureEdition: No officially dated edition or next departure of the target programme was located for December 2026–June 2028 as of 2026-11-15. CTI markets custom programmes rather than an announced recurring event. Its partner publishes an undated four-day Toronto incentive idea; DAY ONE through DAY FOUR are itinerary days, not calendar dates. Toronto and Montréal are separately marketed destinations; a combined itinerary is unverified.
findings.hotelProductFit: Inference using the supplied hotel capacities: prospect for Toronto-only incentive stays, executive/VIP lodging or approximately 15–109 peak-room groups, subject to an actual brief and availability; this range is a sales target, not published CTI demand. A 157-room city hotel can fit a modest Toronto leg but cannot be presumed exclusive housing for a 2,000+ convention. The official hotel page places it near Harbourfront, Rogers Centre and MTCC, relevant to the sample’s city activities. It is not a Montréal or wilderness-resort base. Restaurant/lounge closure is officially disclosed; do not promise the sample’s rooftop hotel dinner, breakfast, banquet service or receptions without separate operational confirmation.
findings.venueCommitments: Actual contracted venue: unknown; Toronto-proper venue commitment: unverified. The sample proposes Cluny Bistro, 360 Restaurant at CN Tower, a Rogers Centre private suite, Eglinton Grand or Fermenting Cellar, and an IYC activity; it also includes an excursion to Niagara Falls outside Toronto. These are illustrative itinerary components, not booking commitments. The hotel is unnamed. The partner directory lists MTCC among Canadian convention centres, not as this programme’s venue.
findings.historicalRotation: No dated edition timeline or destination rotation was established. CTI’s undated client testimonials separately mention a Montréal programme and a Banff event; neither establishes the target programme’s dates, recurrence, hotel or rotation. Geographic coverage is not edition history.
findings.accommodationSourcing: Verified intermediary pathway: CTI states, "We provide site selection, venue selection, hotel property selection" for meetings, events and conferences. Its sample says "Arrival at Toronto Pearson International Airport & transfer to hotel by coach" but names no hotel. No edition-specific housing bureau, host hotel, room block, hotel list or open RFP was located. Every named accommodation hotel in the target materials: none. CTI also describes a confidential annual FIT tariff catalogue of host properties; that is an individual-travel product, not evidence of a group block or an invitation to bid. Hotel sourcing remains unconfirmed, not open.
findings.organizationStructure: Canadian Tours International / CTI Destination Management is a commercial destination management company, not an association or a verified owner of the proposed event series. CTI says it has provided destination management since 1979, is owned and operated by Terry Engesser, and has its head office in Toronto with representatives in Montréal, Vancouver, Calgary and Halifax. Its role includes hotel and venue selection for clients; the end corporate client and contracting buyer for a future programme are unknown.
findings.competitiveLimitations: No incumbent accommodation hotel, exclusive housing arrangement, overflow need, sell-out or displacement was evidenced. CTI offers multiple Canadian destinations, so a Toronto booking is not guaranteed. The sample’s hotel-restaurant dinner and breakfasts create an operational fit risk because the hotel’s official page says "Restaurant and Lounge closed until further notice." This does not prove all meeting catering is unavailable; verify separately.
findings.recommendedSalesAction: Approach Michelle Kenny at the publicly listed michellek@ctidmc.com, copying or escalating to Terry Engesser at terrye@ctidmc.com. Offer a Toronto supplier introduction/site inspection, not a bid for a fictitious edition. Ask whether any December 2026–June 2028 Toronto briefs require a city hotel, and request dates, Toronto nights, peak rooms, budget, breakfast/F&B needs, transport, incumbent properties, selection timetable and the actual contracting party. Present the supplied 157-room product for modest groups or a Toronto leg; disclose restaurant/lounge closure and validate catering before proposing functions.
findings.currentEditionAccessibility: There is no verified current dated edition to access and no documented open inventory. Published CTI contact channels permit account-level outreach, not a claim of an accessible hotel block or live RFP. Do not retain the earlier SALES_READY label as an event qualification.
findings.futureCompetitiveCapturePotential: Inference: CTI’s explicit hotel-selection service creates a credible future supplier-introduction route for Toronto programmes. Seek consideration before a client brief is contracted; distinguish that potential from announced demand or verified annual recurrence. No forecast rooms, conversion probability or repeat cycle can be supported.
